paragraphs.text: Conversation-scoped document browser for DeepSeek Harness: every document your conversations produce
, grouped by conversation, searchable and previewable.
# dsh-doc-panel

A conversation-scoped document browser for **DeepSeek Harness**: every document your
conversations p

roduce — organized by the conversation that produced it, searchable and
previewable, without leaving

organized by the conversation that produced it, searchable and
previewable, without leaving the app.
**English** · 简体中文
## Why

Agent conversations produce real deliverables: Markdown reports, single-file HTML
dashboards, PDFs,

spreadsheets, Word documents. They pile up in one workspace (or a few),
and there is no built-in pla

ce to see what a particular conversation created, find last
week's report, or keep the files you car
e about within reach.

dsh-doc-panel adds one **Documents** panel to the Harness sidebar. It indexes the
documents each con

versation produced, groups them under that conversation, and gives you
the same three things a file

manager gives you: a place to browse, a way to search, and
a short list of favorites.
## Features

- **Conversation folders** — one card per conversation showing its summary outside the
folder: docum

ent count, total size, relative update time and type mix.
- **Dashboard overview** — KPI tiles for c

onversations, documents, favorites and the
last seven days (with a small bar sparkline), a document-

type donut, and a
recently-updated list.
- **Instant search** — filters conversation titles, documen

t names and paths as you
type. It is client-side; document *contents* are not indexed or searched.
-

**Favorites** — star a document from any list or from the preview header. Favorites
persist to disk

and survive restarts; files that disappeared stay listed as
unavailable and cannot be opened.
- **I

nline previews** — rendered Markdown, sandboxed HTML pages, embedded PDF, plain
text/source view, an

d open/download cards for Office documents. Markdown and HTML have
an explicit preview/source toggle

.
- **Accurate grouping** — documents are discovered from session-log references
(`write`, `edit`, `

present`, write-capable tool arguments) plus a filtered workspace
scan. Subagent sessions are folded

into their root conversation.
- **Native look** — styled only with Harness theme tokens, so light a

nd dark themes both
work and the panel sits naturally beside the other Harness pages. Charts are pur

e
SVG/CSS; no chart library.
- **Quiet by design** — no network requests, no telemetry, no runtime d

ependencies, no
build step. The Host half uses Node builtins only.
- **Bilingual UI** — English and
Simplified Chinese, following the Harness locale.
## How it works

The plugin has a Host half (`index.js`, Node) and a Client half (`client.js`, React in the
Harness W
eb app), wired by `cordis.patch.yml` — no build step, no bundler.

- The Host reads the session corpus through the `sessionQuery` service and reduces each
session log

to compact signals: title, first/last time, turn windows and document path
references.
- It scans ea

ch conversation's workspace for files matching the configured extensions
(skipping harness internals

such as `node_modules`, `.git`, `.asar` trees, dot
directories and scratch files).
- Every file is

attributed by a four-tier rule: explicit reference → reference path
mentioned by a write-capable too

l → turn time window around the file's mtime → whole
session window. Files that cannot be attributed

are not listed.
- Child/subagent sessions fold into their root conversation, so a delegated agent's

documents appear under the conversation that spawned it.
- The resulting index is cached in memory,

persisted atomically as JSON, and warmed on
startup; `POST api/dsh-doc-panel/list` serves it, while

`read`/`file` serve previews
from an allow-listed set of indexed paths.
- The Client registers one

sidebar entry and one main panel, renders the dashboard and
previews, and runs HTML previews in a `s

andbox="allow-scripts allow-downloads"` iframe
(no same-origin access).
Details and the data-flow diagram: docs/architecture.md.
## Privacy & security

- **No network, no telemetry.** The plugin makes no outbound requests and embeds no
analytics, crash

reporting or update checks. Your browser only talks to your own
Harness server over the existing au

thenticated session.
- **Reads stay local.** It reads session history through Harness services and w

orkspace
file metadata matching your extension list; file contents are read only when you
preview a

document.
- **Writes are minimal.** Only two files: an index cache and a favorites store, both
under

`<defaultDirectory>/.dsh-doc-panel/` (both overridable, both safe to delete).
- **Preview routes ar

e allow-listed.** `read` and `file` only serve paths present in the
current index; they cannot be us

ed to read arbitrary files.
- **HTML is sandboxed.** HTML previews run with `allow-scripts` but with

out
`allow-same-origin`, so a document cannot touch the Harness DOM, cookies, storage or
authenticat

ed API. Scripts inside a previewed HTML file can still make their own
network requests under normal
browser rules — preview only documents you trust.
Full threat model and the exact read/write surfaces: docs/privacy.md.
## Limitations

- The Markdown renderer is intentionally a pragmatic subset: no setext headings, no
reference-style

links, and raw inline HTML is displayed as text (never executed).
- Relative assets referenced from

Markdown are not served; images resolve through the
raw-file route only for absolute paths (or `http

(s)`/`data:` URLs).
- HTML previews run in a sandboxed frame without same-origin access, so pages th

at depend
on same-origin storage or APIs can misbehave.
- Documents must still exist on disk: delete

d or moved files drop out of the index, and
a preview requires the file to be readable.
- Attributio

n is heuristic. A file copied in from outside the session, or renamed/edited
long after the turn tha

t created it, can be assigned to the wrong conversation — or not
listed at all.
- Legacy v0 session

logs may be unreadable by the current Harness; those scans return a
partial index with `diag.complet

e: false`.
- `.csv` and `.txt` are not indexed by default (they are usually intermediate files); add
them through `extensions` if you want them.
